The '''Elsasser number''', Λ, is a dimensionless number in [[magnetohydrodynamics]] that represents the ratio of magnetic forces to the Coriolis force.{{sfnp|Gubbins|Herrero-Bervera|2007| p=299}}

<math display="block">\Lambda = \frac{\sigma B^2}{\rho \Omega}</math>

where σ is the [[Electrical conductivity|conductivity]] of the fluid, ''B'' is the [[magnetic field]], ρ is the density of the fluid, and Ω is the rate of rotation of the body.

== Applications ==
This number is useful when studying the [[linear stability]] of an [[accretion disc]] to the [[magnetorotational instability]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lesur |first=Geoffroy R. J. |date=February 2021 |title=Magnetohydrodynamics of protoplanetary discs |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-plasma-physics/article/magnetohydrodynamics-of-protoplanetary-discs/0557575DE812AAA9DD8324A5E6F6165A |journal=Journal of Plasma Physics |language=en |volume=87 |issue=1 |pages=205870101 |doi=10.1017/S0022377820001002 |issn=0022-3778|arxiv=2007.15967 }}</ref>
